newsitem.title: MEXICO: Zedillo says Mexico maturing politically.
newsitem.headline: Zedillo says Mexico maturing politically.

text.p: Mexican President Ernesto Zedillo said on Sunday that elections scheduled for July 6 will show Mexico is maturing both politically and democratically.
"The country is ready to make significant political advances to reconfirm and consolidate a full democratic life," Zedillo said in an interview with the pro-government television network Televisa.

Mexico stages key mid-term elections next Sunday to choose a new congress, a quarter of the senate, six state governors, and for the first time, a mayor of Mexico City, which previously was a presidential appointment.

Zedillo, whose Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) has held the presidency, most governorships and congressional control for the past 68 years, said the process of political and electoral change the country is going through "something quiet extraordinary".
Polls show the opposition left-leaning Party of the Democratic Revolution (PRD) ahead in the Mexico City mayoral race and also the PRI in grave danger of losing its congressional majority.

Mexico has undergone substantial electoral reform in recent years. One important change was to create an independent Federal Election Institute, an autonomous body overseeing votes. Fraud in elections is not uncommon in Mexico.
Zedillo said he was not worried about the elections and said he hoped Mexicans would turn out in force to exercise their votes. "It would be terrible if people did not vote," he added.
